preconditions.description: The number of towns n is an integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(1 <= a_i <= n for a_i in a) and all(a_i != i for i in range(1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: The input list a has exactly n elements, each a_i is an integer between 1 and n inclusive, and no road points to itself (a_i ≠ i).

postconditions.description: The output is a string representing the number of valid subsets of roads to flip (modulo 10^9 + 7) such that the resulting directed graph has no directed cycles. The count is computed as follows: For each possible subset of roads to flip, the resulting graph must be a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

postconditions.expression: count_valid_flips(n, a) == sum(1 for mask in range(0, 2**n) if is_dag(n, a, mask))
postconditions.description: The function count_valid_flips(n, a) counts all subsets of roads (represented by a bitmask) where flipping the roads in the subset results in a DAG. A DAG is defined as a directed graph with no directed cycles of length ≥ 1. The bitmask is an integer where the i-th bit (0-based) indicates whether the i-th road (1-based) is flipped.

postconditions.expression: is_dag(n, a, mask) == not any(has_directed_cycle(n, a, mask))
postconditions.description: The helper predicate is_dag(n, a, mask) checks if the resulting graph after flipping roads according to mask has no directed cycles. A directed cycle exists if there is a sequence of distinct towns A_1, A_2, ..., A_k (k ≥ 1) such that for every 1 ≤ i < k there is a directed road from A_i to A_{i+1} and a directed road from A_k to A_1.

postconditions.expression: has_directed_cycle(n, a, mask) == any(all(1 <= A_i <= n for A_i in cycle) and len(set(cycle)) == len(cycle) and all((A_i, A_{i+1}) in get_edges(n, a, mask) for i in range(len(cycle) - 1)) and (cycle[-1], cycle[0]) in get_edges(n, a, mask) for cycle in all_possible_cycles(n))
postconditions.description: The helper predicate has_directed_cycle(n, a, mask) checks if there exists any directed cycle in the graph after flipping roads according to mask. The edges are determined by the original roads and the flips specified by mask. A cycle is a sequence of distinct towns where each consecutive pair (and the last to first) forms a directed edge in the graph.

postconditions.expression: get_edges(n, a, mask) == {(i, a_i if not (mask & (1 << (i - 1))) else a_i) for i in range(1, n + 1)} | {(a_i, i) for i in range(1, n + 1) if (mask & (1 << (i - 1)))}
postconditions.description: The helper function get_edges(n, a, mask) returns the set of directed edges in the graph after flipping roads according to mask. For each road i (1-based), if the i-th bit in mask is set, the edge is reversed from (i, a_i) to (a_i, i); otherwise, it remains (i, a_i).
